ls: List the files in a folder.
the ones whose names start with .
grep: Print the lines of FILE that contain WORD.
Capitals count: Gold is not gold.
open: Open a picture in its viewer window.
man: Show the manual page for COMMAND.
head: HEAD(1)

Print the first N lines (10 if not given).
pwd: Print the folder you are in.
ps: List running programs and their numbers.
cp: Copy a file. Client files aren't yours:
copy them home (~) to change them.
chmod: chmod +r FILE   let it be read
chmod +x FILE   let a script run
Only works on files you own (in ~).
kill: Stop a program. Windows show their
number in the title bar. Programs
without windows only show in ps.
sort: Print a file's lines in order.
unzip: Unpack an archive here, or into FOLDER.
Locked archives ask for a password.
su: Become USER. Asks for USER's password.
exit   go back to being you
sudo: Asks for YOUR password, and only works
write: Send a line to USER's terminal.

help_page: HOW TO PLAY: HELP THEM BOUNCE BACK
Every AI went dark. First you fix things for people. Then you teach them to fix things themselves.
1. Dig: type commands in the terminal to find the right file.
2. Shape: open it, then drag the window's edge or corner. The picture stretches to fit.
3. SNAP the picture (button in its title bar) to attach it.
4. Send. Wrong answers bounce back. Read the reply and try again.
5. Teach: when a client wants to learn, type write NAME COMMAND. Their own machine runs exactly what you send, typos included.
COMMANDS (type them, press Enter)
ls            list files (ls -a: hidden ones too)
open FILE     open a picture
grep WORD FILE  find lines with WORD. Capitals count.
cd FOLDER     go into a folder (cd .. back up, cd ~ home)
man COMMAND   the manual for a command
cp FILE DEST  copy a file (client files: copy them home first)
chmod +x FILE let a script run (+r: let it be read)
ps / kill PID list programs / stop one (numbers are in title bars)
sort FILE     lines in order (-n by number, -r reversed)
unzip FILE -d ~  unpack an archive into your home folder
su USER / sudo COMMAND  become someone / run as administrator
write NAME CMD  send a command to a client's machine (teach them)
help          the short list in the terminal
KEYS
Tab completes names. Up/Down repeat old commands.
Esc: leave the terminal for the pictures. Then Tab picks one, arrows stretch,
Ctrl+arrows move, S snaps, T traces, Enter sends, Esc goes back.
BUTTONS
TRACE (some jobs): see-through, to lay one picture on another.
SNAPSHOT: drag a box; every picture fully inside is attached.
text: big / normal, radio: on / off.
